primitives.name: Launch Readiness Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Owned Metrics Readiness score, blocker count, test evidence, customer impact, revenue/trust/support metrics relevant to the department.
primitives.assumptions: The score reflects the probability that a deployment meets all operational, compliance, and performance requirements without failure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At $R \rightarrow 0$, the system is deemed 'not ready' and deployment must be halted; at $R \rightarrow 1$, the system is considered fully validated.

layer2.mapping: The Launch Readiness Score maps directly to a posterior probability in a conformal inference framework, where $R$ represents the empirical coverage of a conformal prediction interval for deployment outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Observed deployment success rates, blocker resolution times, and automated test pass/fail ratios

primitives.name: Definition Of Ready
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Definition Of Ready The build has an owner, source files, duplicate gate, approval gate, test plan, rollback plan, and acceptance criteria.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$O_i$': 'Boolean indicator for each requirement (dimensionless)', '$D_{ready}$': 'Binary readiness flag (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: All prerequisite components ($O_i$) must be present and valid for a build to be considered ready for deployment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If any single requirement fails ($O_i = 0$), then $D_{ready} = 0$, indicating immediate blockage.

layer2.mapping: This definition corresponds to a conjunctive kernel in a derived decision-theoretic model, where $D_{ready}$ acts as a gating function for proceeding through the release pipeline.
layer2.telemetry: Count of satisfied requirements, time-to-ready metrics, and percentage of builds meeting all criteria

primitives.name: Definition Of Done
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Definition Of Done The change is implemented or explicitly blocked, tested, documented, screenshot/source verified if relevant, and reflected in the command center.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$T_j$': 'Boolean indicator for each completion task (dimensionless)', '$D_{done}$': 'Binary done flag (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Every required task ($T_j$) must be completed successfully for a change to be marked as 'done'.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure of any task ($T_j = 0$) results in $D_{done} = 0$, necessitating further work before closure.

layer2.mapping: This mirrors a derived kernel in a workflow control system, where $D_{done}$ serves as a terminal condition for a software development lifecycle state transition.
layer2.telemetry: Task completion percentages, cycle time per change, and documentation coverage scores

primitives.name: Launch Blocker Triage
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Tools Needed Repo search, test scripts, browser/screenshot tooling, source checks, spreadsheets/ledgers, and command-center queue.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$C_k$': 'Boolean compliance indicator for each category (dimensionless)', '$B_{blocker}$': 'Binary blocker flag (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: A single non-compliant category ($C_k = 1$) triggers a total blocker status, halting progression through the release pipeline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If any compliance check fails ($C_k = 1$), then $B_{blocker} = 1$, forcing immediate remediation.

layer2.mapping: This triage process implements a fault-tree analysis kernel, where $B_{blocker}$ acts as a safety interlock preventing unsafe deployments.
layer2.telemetry: Blocker frequency, severity-weighted blocker counts, and mean time to clear blockers
